title: Large-Scale Cell Production Based on GMP-Grade Dissolvable Porous Microcarriers
protocol: Isolate primary human UCMSCs from Wharton's jelly according to the reported method.
Inoculate 6 x 10^5 human UCMSCs in one T75 flask with 15 mL of complete SF hMSC culture medium.
Ensure uniform seeding through a figure-eight movement of the flask.
Culture at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 cell culture incubator to 80%-90% confluency.
Decant the cell culture medium.
Rinse the cells twice with 3-5 mL of phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add 2 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1-2 min until most cells have become round and detached from the flask.
Add 3 mL of SF hMSC culture medium to terminate digestion.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 179 x g for 5 min.
Decant the supernatant.
Rinse the cell pellet with PBS twice.
Resuspend the cells in around 3-5 mL of SF hMSC culture medium for seeding to microcarriers in bioreactors.
Check the cell viability and ensure it is >90% viable.
Inoculate 2 x 10^6-3 x 10^6 HEK293T or Vero cells into each T75 flask with DMEM containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) for HEK293T and 10% newborn calf serum (NBS) for Vero cells.
Harvest the cells as described in steps 1.3-1.4.
Resuspend the harvested cells in 3-5 mL of DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Rinse the glass vessel thoroughly with running deionized (DI) water once.
Disassemble all stainless tubes and impellers from the headplate.
Immerse them in DI water.
Sonicate with an ultrasonic cleaner at 40 kHz and 60 °C for 1 h to clean thoroughly.
Check all O-rings are intact and in place according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Replace any worn or torn O-rings before assembly if necessary.
Add 7 L of 0.5 M NaOH solution into the 5 L vessel, and place the headplate with tubes assembled on the rim of the vessel to immerse the tubes in the NaOH solution.
Let it stand for 12 h or overnight to remove endotoxins from the tubes and glass vessel.
Remove the headplate and decant the NaOH solution into a proper waste bottle.
Rinse the vessel, the headplate, and its parts thoroughly with endotoxin-free DI water or water for injection.
Add 2 L (5 L) of PBS to the vessel.
Reassemble all parts and bolt the headplate to the metal frame according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Fit a Closed System Consumable Pack to the appropriate stainless steel parts/tubes/ports on the headplate according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Clamp all Robert clamps on the tubes.
Slip silicone tubes onto the tips of the hemostats to prevent piercing the silicone tubes.
Avoid clamping C-flex tubes included in this kit, clamp only on the silicone tubes.
Leave one tube with an 0.22 μm air vent filter at the end connected to the condenser unclamped for pressure relief during autoclaving.
Prepare 250 mL of 0.1 M NaOH solution in a 500 mL GL 45 glass bottle.
Fit the GL 45 Multiport Connector Screw Cap with two ports onto the glass bottle.
Connect a 180 mm long silicone tube to one port on the lower side of the cap, ensuring it touches the bottom of the bottle.
Connect another piece of silicone tube, 500 mm longer than the previous one, to the same port on the upper side of the cap and connect it to a drip feed port on the 5 L vessel headplate.
Connect a 0.22 μm air vent filter to the other port on the screw cap.
Perform a two-point calibration on the pH probe as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Insert the pH probe into the vessel in the appropriate PG13 port.
Insert the dissolved oxygen (DO) probe into the vessel in the appropriate PG13 port.
Insert the live cell count probes into the vessel in the appropriate PG13,5 ports.
Screw all probes tight onto the headplate.
Perform an airtightness check of the fully assembled vessel according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Maintain a pressure of 0.4 bar ± 0.01 bar for at least 30 min.
Slowly release the pressure after the system passes the test.
Carefully search for leak points and reinforce the vessel assembly if the airtightness test fails.
Autoclave the fully assembled vessel with the consumable kit at 15 psi and 121 °C for 60 min.
Check all air vent filters to ensure they are intact and dry after autoclaving.
Change the air vent filters if they are wet, and autoclave the entire vessel again.
Transfer the autoclaved vessel into a cleanroom, and wait for it to completely cool to room temperature.
Insert the temperature probe into the thermowell tube.
Connect the cables for the motor from the controller to the respective parts on the vessel.
Connect the cables for the pH probe from the controller to the respective parts on the vessel.
Connect the cables for the DO probe from the controller to the respective parts on the vessel.
Wrap the heat mat around the vessel tightly.
Unclamp the Robert clamps on the flexible tubes on the exhaust gas condenser.
Unclamp the Robert clamps on the flexible tubes on the ring sparger.
Unclamp the Robert clamps on the flexible tube at the drip feed port for NaOH.
Unclamp the Robert clamps on the flexible tube at the air overlay port.
Turn on the controller and log in.
Enter parameters listed in Table 1 into the system according to manufacturer's instructions.
Click on Start, and name the experiment to start the bioreactor.
Allow the bioreactor to run for at least 12 h or overnight.
Install a 0.13 in x 0.25 in silicone tube on pump 1 with one end dipping into a bottle of water.
Insert the other end of the silicone tube from pump 1 into a measuring cylinder.
Set the pump rotation speed to 300 rpm for pump 1 and time for 1 min.
Note the amount of water dispensed by pump 1 into the measuring cylinder.
Install a 0.13 in x 0.25 in silicone tube on pump 2 with one end dipping into a bottle of water.
Insert the other end of the silicone tube from pump 2 into a measuring cylinder.
Set the pump rotation speed to 300 rpm for pump 2 and time for 1 min.
Note the amount of water dispensed by pump 2 into the measuring cylinder.
Prepare 500 mL of SF hMSC culture medium according to manufacturer's instructions.
Replace the cap of the cell culture medium bottle with a disposable C-Flex EZ Top container closure and compatible cap inside a biosafety cabinet (BSC).
Weld the outlet tube on the bottle of medium to the inlet C-flex tube on the bottle of 10 g pre-sterilized W01 microcarriers for MSC.
Install a section of the tube onto pump 1 of the bioreactor controller and set the pump rotation to 300 rpm.
Pump in all the culture medium from the bottle into the bottle of microcarriers.
Store these microcarriers at 4 °C until use on day 0.
Prepare a 2 L glass bottle for waste collection, fit it with a GL 45 Multiport Connector Screw Cap with two ports and connect 30 mm C-Flex tubes to both ports.
Autoclave the waste bottle assembly to sterilize.
Weld the C-flex tube from one of the ports on the waste bottle to the harvest tube on the headplate of the bioreactor vessel using a tube welder.
Stop the temperature, pH, and DO control on the bioreactor controller temporarily.
Install the silicone tube attached to the harvest tube onto peristaltic pump 2 in the correct liquid flow direction.
Fully dispense all the PBS from the vessel into the waste bottle.
Dislodge the tube from the pump.
Seal and disconnect the waste bottle.
Unclamp any Robert clamps on the flexible tubes involved in liquid flow before transferring liquids.
Reclamp tubes after completing liquid transfer before sealing and disconnecting.
Prep 7 L (30 L) of complete SF hMSC medium.
Replace each original bottle cap with a disposable C-Flex EZ Top container closure and compatible cap.
Weld a Single-Use Filtration Module to one port on the 10 L (50 L) Single-Use Storage Bag.
Perform cap replacement inside a BSC.
Filter and transfer culture medium to the storage bag, one bottle at a time.
Weld bottles of cell culture medium to the other end of the capsule filter.
Use pump on bioreactor controller for filtration and transfer.
Designate the prepared bag as the feed bag.
Weld one outlet port from the feed bag to the C-flex tube on the feed tube of the headplate.
Install the welded tube to pump 1 on the bioreactor controller.
Weld the other outlet port from the feed bag to the bleed tube.
Install this tube to pump 2 on the bioreactor controller in the correct direction of liquid flow.
Set the pump 1 speed to 300 rpm.
Stop the pump after dispensing 1 L (5 L) of medium from the feed bag into the vessel.
Seal and disconnect the tube connecting the feed bag to the feed tube on the headplate.
Weld the C-Flex tube from the bottle of the dispersed microcarriers prepared in step 2.18 to the feed tube.
Pump all the content from the bottle into the vessel.
Seal and disconnect the empty bottle of microcarrier suspension.
Disinfect the entire surface of the bottle with 75% ethanol.
Place the disinfected bottle in a BSC to use as a cell suspension transfer bottle.
Ensure that the temperature shown on the controller reaches a steady state of 37 °C.
Resuspend 2.5 x 10^8 hMSCs in 500 mL of SF medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to the empty bottle previously containing the microcarrier suspension.
Weld the C-Flex tube from the bottle now containing the cell suspension to the feed port on the headplate.
Pump all of the contents from the bottle into the vessel to initiate cell inoculation to the microcarriers.
Seal and disconnect the empty bottle.
Re-weld the feed port from the feed bag to the feed tube on the headplate.

Adjust the agitation settings on the controller to allow intermittent agitation for enhanced inoculation efficiency of hMSCs by setting V1 = 35 (30) rpm/5 min, V2 = 0 rpm/25 min, number of cycles = 12 (24), and final agitation speed = 35 (30) rpm.
Set up an automated medium supplement and exchange regime on the bioreactor controller in the Medium Exchange interface.
Unclamp any Robert clamps on flexible tubes involved in liquid flow.
Keep unclamped clamps open throughout the entire culture process.
Connect disposable sampling bags via Luer connectors at desired time points for sampling.
Aliquot 2-3 mL of sample and discard to ensure accuracy.
Aliquot 10 mL of actual sample into a new sampling bag each time.
Sanitize Luer connectors with 75% ethanol before and after making or breaking connections.
Transfer samples to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Take 200 μL of cell-laden microcarrier suspension for staining.
Stain cells using Calcein-AM/PI Cell Double Staining according to manufacturer's instructions.
Observe stained cells under a fluorescence microscope.
Sediment microcarriers by gravity, which takes about 5-10 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant after sedimentation.
Test glucose concentration in the sample with a glucose meter as per manufacturer's instructions.
Plot a glucose level graph.
Incubate the sedimented cell-laden microcarriers with a freshly prepared 3-5 mL of 1 mg/mL digest solution at 37 °C for 20-30 min to fully dissolve the microcarriers.
Count the cells after staining with AO/PI with an automated fluorescence cell analyzer.
Plot a cell growth curve.
Correlate with the real-time live cell growth curve generated on the controller.
Prepare 50 mL (or 200 mL) of digest solution at 30 mg/mL on day 4 or day 5 of culture.
Sterile-filter the digest solution with a 0.22 μm capsule filter.
Further dilute the filtered digest solution in 500 mL (or 2 L) of Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS) with calcium and magnesium.
Transfer the diluted solution to a 3 L disposable storage bag.
Harvest cells aiming for at least 1.0 x 10^9-1.2 x 10^9 cells for the first-tier expansion and 1.0 x 10^10 cells for the second-tier expansion.
If the cells grow faster, harvest on day 4; if not, harvest on day 5.
Do not extend beyond day 5 for harvesting.
Set agitation speed to 0 on the controller for the microcarriers to settle.
Wait until the microcarriers have settled, which usually takes about 20 minutes.
Turn off the automated medium exchange protocol.
Stop the temperature control on the bioreactor controller.
Stop the pH control on the bioreactor controller.
Stop the dissolved oxygen (DO) control on the bioreactor controller.
Manually start pump 2 at 300 rpm on the controller.
Dispense supernatant into the feed regime to leave about 1 L of culture suspension in the vessel.
Seal and totally disconnect the feed bag.
Weld the bag of freshly prepared digest solution from step 3.15 to the feed tube.
Pump all the contents into the vessel.
Start the agitation speed at 45 (40) rpm.
Ensure that the temperature control is maintaining the temperature at 37 °C.
Take 1 mL of the sample with a sterile Luer lock syringe at 30 min.
Subsequently take samples every 5-10 min to observe under a bright-field microscope.
Check the dissolution of the microcarriers.
Weld one 3 L storage bag (two 3 L storage bags for the 15 L bioreactor) to the harvest tube.
Pump out the cell suspension completely using pump 2 at 300 rpm.
Prepare 1 L (3.5 L) of saline containing 1% human serum albumin (HSA).
Prepare 500 mL of complete SF medium (500 mL of cell cryopreservation buffer, a formulation of 10% dimethyl sulfate (DMSO) and 90% SF medium).
Install a Disposable Cell Processing Kit to the instrument according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Weld the bags of cell suspension, wash buffer, and SF medium (cryopreservation buffer) to the Disposable Cell Processing Kit.
Follow all the instructions displayed on the user interface to initialize the kit.
Check the integrity and proper installation of the kit.
Enter parameters listed in Table 3 for cell washing with wash buffer and resuspension in SF medium into the software.
Start the wash and resuspension process using the automated system.
Take a sample of cells from the centrifuge chamber as indicated by the cell processing system.
Calculate the cell density with an automated cell analyzer according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Adjust the resuspension volume for a density of 2 x 10^6 cells/mL or a maximum total volume of 250 mL.
Seal and disconnect the cell transfer bag from the Disposable Cell Processing Kit after the system has aspirated the cells out from the chamber.
Readjust the cell density to 2 x 10^6 cells/mL with complete SF medium in a larger cell transfer bag/medium storage bag if necessary.
Resuspend the cells in 250 mL of cryopreservation buffer for seed cells for the second-tier expansion in the 15 L bioreactor.
Transfer 2,000 mL of cryopreservation buffer together with the 250 mL of resuspended cells to a 3 L cell transfer bag.
Weld the transfer bag to a Disposable Fill&Finish Consumable Kit.
Assemble the Disposable Fill&Finish Consumable Kit to the cell filling system and turn on the pre-cooling system according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Set the system to fill 20 mL/bag with a total of 20 bags per batch.
Seal and disconnect these bags from the kit, and follow standard cryopreservation procedures.
Weld a new set of 20 cryopreservation bags to the Disposable Fill&Finish Consumable Kit.
Repeat the fill and finish procedure until all the cells are aliquoted.
Follow standard procedures to cryopreserve these cells.
Sample the harvested hMSCs from the dissolvable microcarriers.
Use a cell processing system for characterization by flow cytometry for the determination of the cell identity following methods described in literature.
Thaw the cryopreserved cells.
Replate the cells on conventional 2D flasks or microplates for further characterization.
Prepare a 5 L bioreactor as mentioned in step 2.
Culture HEK293T cells with sterile G02 microcarriers instead of W01.
Install a special perfusion tube in the bioreactor to replace the bleed tube.
Prepare 20 g of G02 microcarriers in DMEM with 10% FBS for the 5 L bioreactor.
Set the day 0 culture volume at 3.5 L (i.e., a final concentration of about 5.71 g/L).
Dispense 2 L of medium into the vessel before adding G02 microcarriers.
Inoculate 500 mL of HEK293T cells at a density of 1.75 x 10^9 cells (i.e., final density of 5 x 10^5 cells/mL).
Activate pump 1 manually for continuous perfusion.
Activate pump 2 manually for continuous perfusion.
Adjust pump speed daily based on calibration.
Use fresh medium as feed for HEK293T cells.
Discard spent medium totally into a waste bottle for HEK293T cells.
For hMSCs, circulate the medium instead of discarding it entirely.
Stop agitation to sediment microcarriers when desired cell density is reached.
Aspirate supernatant out of perfusion tube as much as possible.
Wash microcarriers with PBS three times.
Feed PBS with a volume three times that of the remaining suspension for washing.
Repeat wash step three times.
Aspirate and discard as much PBS as possible in the final wash.
Feed in 3.5 L of 1x recombinant trypsin at 37 °C and 60 rpm agitation speed to detach cells from microcarriers.
Terminate detachment after 45 min when more than 80% of the cells have detached, with an equal amount of complete medium.
Transfer directly to a prepared 15 L vessel for second-tier expansion through the harvest port.
Prepare V01 microcarriers by transferring lyophilized microcarriers into the bioreactor vessel together with PBS at a concentration of 20 mg/mL.
Assemble and sterilize the vessel as mentioned in protocol section 2, but autoclave for 30 min.
Exchange the supernatant with basic DMEM two times using bleed and feed tubes after sterilization.
Add complete DMEM containing 10% NBS to 50%-75% of the volume of the vessel.
Use 24 g of V01 microcarriers for a 4 L culture of Vero cells (final concentration of 6 g/L).
Inoculate 500 mL of 4 x 10^9 Vero cells (final density of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL).
Follow steps 6.3-6.6 for the culture process parameters and passaging to second-tier expansion in the 15 L stirred-tank bioreactor.
